title: Completeness and faithful scalar restriction for integral objects
statement: Fix a prime l and a finite extension E of Q_l, with R=O_E and its uniformizer ideal I. Use the actual completed integral coefficient sheaves, strict system calculus, and the normalized constant scalar restrictions H and U [def-sf-constant-completed-reduction-transport, def-sf-integral-system-operations]. For any scheme W and any M in D(W,Rhat) satisfying finiteTorConstructibleIntegral [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], the actual constant quotient-completion unit eta_(H M) is invertible. For every such N, H induces an injective map Hom(M,N) -> Hom(H M,H N). No faithfulness is asserted outside the complete subcategory, and there is no scheme-finiteness or nonempty-site assumption.

source.place: Tags 099I, 099L and 099N; parent Steps 1 and 9. T9 site-specific specialization of complete constant/completed equivalence and its unit normalization.

proof.text: Extract IsSfDerivedComplete from the sfIntegralConstructible component of finiteTorConstructibleIntegral: its actual quotient units exhibit M as the derived limit of its reduction tower. Over the Noetherian DVR, the quotient/Koszul comparison identifies this with intrinsic derived completeness. The flat constant/completed equivalence identifies the uniformizer kernel ideals and positive quotient sheaves and carries M to a complete constant-coefficient object.

Transport along the fixed exact small-site module equivalence used in ordinaryH. Its quotient comparisons preserve the full quotient diagram, total right derived limit and augmentation. The completion-unit criterion identifies the constant intrinsic completeness predicate with invertibility of the actual sfCbcSite.unit, proving the first claim.

For M,N both complete, restrict the constant/completed equivalence to these objects. Its faithful functor detects equality of maps. The subsequent small-site exact equivalence is faithful on derived categories, and its composite is H by definition. Thus H.map is injective on Hom(M,N). Zero objects and the empty site require no additional hypotheses.

lean.statement:
theorem completeIntegralConstantRestriction (W : Scheme.{u})
    (M : IntegralSystemRealization.Integral l E W)
    (hM : finiteTorConstructibleIntegral l E W M) :
    IsIso (((sfCbcSite W).unit _
      (sfCbcModelIdeal (GeneratorReduction.constantDatum l E))).app
        ((GeneratorReduction.H l E W).obj M)) ∧
    ∀ (N : IntegralSystemRealization.Integral l E W),
      finiteTorConstructibleIntegral l E W N →
        Function.Injective ((GeneratorReduction.H l E W).map (X := M) (Y := N))
